rationale: healing-agent is a general-purpose Python self-healing code library that catches exceptions at runtime, captures detailed context (stack traces, local/global variables, function arguments), sends context to an LLM (multi-provider: Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, LiteLLM), receives a fix, validates syntax, creates a backup, and rewrites the function in-place via AST. It addresses the 'self-healing' pipeline concern directly. However, it is not a scraping pipeline component: no JSON-LD extraction, browser automation, script generation for scraping, stealth, queue, fuzzy matching, or full-text search. Its relevance to a laptop-specs scraping pipeline is indirect—it could heal broken scraper code but is not purpose-built for scraping. Architectural depth is moderate: decorator-based interception, multi-provider AI broker, context capture with secret redaction, AST-based code replacement, configurable persistence. No formal architecture docs exist beyond README/CHANGELOG. Tests cover redactor, JSON decode error handling, and integration examples. Tier C reflects niche relevance to one pipeline concern with decent implementation depth but no scraping-specific utility.
limitations: Not a scraping pipeline component; relevance to Veridian is indirect (could heal scraper code at runtime)
No JSON-LD/Schema.org extraction, browser automation, script generation for scrapers, stealth, queue, fuzzy matching, or full-text search
No architecture/design documents beyond README and CHANGELOG
Experimental agent_tools (install_missing_module, check_env_variables, list_files_functions, json_fixer) are marked unused
Self-healing operates at Python function level, not at selector/DOM level for web scraping
AUTO_FIX mutates source files at runtime—risky for production scrapers
Single-author project (Máté Benyovszky), alpha status (Development Status :: 3 - Alpha)
